newsitem.title: FRANCE: Perfume sales in France seen up slightly in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Perfume sales in France seen up slightly in 1996.

text.p: Sales of perfume in France rose by two to three percent last year, but exports may have risen by as much as 10 percent, Pierre Bisson, financial director of the French perfume industry federation, said.
Perfume sales in France totalled 29.73 billion francs ($5.6 billion) in 1995, and exports accounted for 29.35 billion, he told Reuters on Tuesday.

"Exports rose (in 1996) with the strengthening of the dollar, but the French market stagnated because of weak customer demand," he said. He said he expected exports to show an increase of between eight and 10 percent for 1997.
Perfume prices rose 1.2 percent last year after a 0.9 percent rise in 1995, he estimated. They are expected to rise between one and two percent in the first half of 1997, he said.
The federation groups 230 firms and Bisson estimated the big houses and brands suffered the most last year. He expects a two percent drop in their perfume sales after a flurry of launches.

He estimated sales of mass market perfumes and beauty products -- around 50 to 55 percent of the products represented by the federation -- were up between three and four percent last year and should continue to rise at a similar pace this year.
Last year was marked by an increase in space in pharmacies, which are expected to show a five percent increase in their sales, Bisson said.
In Europe, Germany remained France's top client but the European market was generally weak. Exports to the United States rebounded and were strong in Asia and Latin America.
Bisson said he expected Asian demand to remain strong this year, and he said demand should recover in Europe.

He said the seasonal nature of perfume sales, previously concentrated during the end-of-year holiday season, appeared to be waning. He said only 12 percent of the sales generated by the industry in 1995 were recorded in December. ($ = 5.301 French Francs)
